header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Another important tool is mechanistic analysis, i.e. studying the model's weights and activations for understanding how it functions, which has been shown to fully explain the behavior of entire neural networks (Nanda et al., 2023; Olah et al., 2020).

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

args.query: mechanistic analysis studying model's weights and activations fully explain behavior of entire neural networks
Nanda mechanistic interpretability progress measures grokking
mechanistic interpretability weights activations neural network behavior
another important tool is mechanistic analysis
interpretability tool mechanistic explain behavior neural networks

Nanda 2023 mechanistic interpretability grokking modular addition
circuits neurons curve detectors reverse engineering vision models
fully explain behavior neural network reverse-engineered algorithm
Olah Cammarata Schubert Goh Petrov Carter

args.quote: Another important tool is mechanistic analysis, i.e. studying the model’s weights and activations for understanding how it functions (Nanda et al., 2023; Olah et al., 2020).
Zoom in: An introduction to circuits. Distill, 5(3), Mar. 2020.

events.delta:
Verdict: not supported

The sentence is a paraphrase of a passage in *Model evaluation for extreme risks* (Shevlane et al., arXiv:2305.15324). The source's own wording is: "Another important tool is mechanistic analysis, i.e. studying the model's weights and activations for understanding how it functions (Nanda et al., 2023; Olah et al., 2020)." That matches the sentence you gave, up to the final clause. (arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p12)

The clause "which has been shown to fully explain the behavior of entire neural networks" does not appear in the source. The source describes mechanistic analysis only as a tool "for understanding how it functions." It does not say the method has been shown to fully explain whole networks. The passage goes on to describe ambitions: studying how a model's goals are represented internally, and detecting when a model's outputs misreport its knowledge. Those are aims, not demonstrated results. (arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p12)

The cited works themselves are not available in the library, so I could not check what they say:
- Olah et al., 2020 appears only in the reference list of the same paper, as "C. Olah, N. Cammarata, L. Schubert, G. Goh, M. Petrov, and S. Carter. Zoom in: An introduction to circuits. Distill, 5(3), Mar. 2020." (arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p18). I did not find its full text.
- Nanda et al., 2023 did not turn up as a document in the library. My searches returned only a reference-list mention in the same paper (arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p17).

So the citation supports only the modest claim that mechanistic analysis studies weights and activations to understand how a model functions. The "fully explain the behavior of entire neural networks" claim is not supported by the library's text, and I could not confirm it from either cited work.
